body.x: AstroX Co., Ltd. (CEO Jeon Boohwan) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

AstroX specializes in developing high-capacity, long-range drones and personal air vehicles (PAVs), positioning itself as a leader in high-performance unmanned and manned aircraft technology. The company boasts engineering and manufacturing capabilities, collaborating with global partners to optimize components such as battery packs and control systems for producing fully integrated aircraft.

AstroX also leverages expertise in CFRP (carbon fiber-reinforced polymer) and aerospace composites, enabling rapid response from development to production. The company aims to commercialize safe and affordable air mobility solutions by applying aerospace certifications to its technologies, supporting reliable operations for all drone service providers.

AstroX’s core technologies include airframe design and structural analysis for optimized safety and performance. Its proprietary vacuum thermal molding and manufacturing techniques for aerospace CFRP composites enhance material lightweight and fuel efficiency. The company also offers advanced power management systems (BMS) for drones, ensuring stable power supply to propulsion systems and custom ground control systems (GCS) for user-specific operation needs.

body.cap: Scale Model of AX-P80D | Photo by AstroX

body.x: At CES 2025, AstroX showcased a scaled model of its high-capacity, long-range air vehicle and screened flight demonstration videos at its booth to highlight its technical capabilities.

The 'AX-P80D,' introduced at CES, features a BLDC motor electric propulsion system with an operational range of 10 km, a flight altitude of 150 meters, and a maximum takeoff weight of 200 kg. With a payload capacity exceeding 50 kg and a flight time of over 30 minutes, it is designed for diverse applications, including firefighting and logistics.

Key features include heat and body temperature management, video transmission capabilities, and specialized lifting mechanisms, such as a drone-specific vertical lift system based on existing ATV winches. The drone also supports modular attachments for firefighting, including a quick-release mechanism for fire suppression modules and a rapid-drop liquid dispersion system ('Bambi Bucket').

AstroX has also developed an amphibious PAV with domestic technology that can operate on land and water. This PAV is suitable for tourism, leisure, and sports, offering an expanded range of applications.

South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport has certified the PAV for ultralight aircraft safety. It has been successfully tested in real environments, including the Han River, Gyeongin Ara Waterway, and Songdo.

body.cap: AstroX demonstrates firefighting capabilities during ship fire scenarios | Photo by AstroX

body.x: AstroX’s self-developed 100 kg payload PAV platform supports various models, including 30 kg and 50 kg payload options, addressing various market demands. With a 30-minute flight time and a 10 km delivery range, these solutions are optimized for island and port logistics.

AstroX’s firefighting drones are particularly notable for their amphibious capabilities. Equipped with a 60 kg fire suppression module, they excel in land and maritime fire suppression, including onboard ship fires. The company’s firefighting solutions have demonstrated outstanding performance and practicality in these challenging scenarios.

AstroX plans to leverage visitor data collected at CES 2025 to engage with potential clients and partners, providing customized proposals and detailed materials to advance collaborative opportunities. The company will also integrate feedback from CES into its product development and improvement processes to create more competitive offerings.

Based on market trends and technological insights gained from CES, AstroX aims to adjust and expand its R&D investments. The company is committed to achieving its goal of developing lightweight aircraft for two passengers by 2030 while exploring further applications in medical transport for emergencies.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
